description: Hospital's 340B-program acquisition cost for one Liletta levonorgestrel IUD, for a 340B-eligible (safety-net/disproportionate-share) hospital
source: AAFCPAs, 'LILETTA IUD May Offer Cost Savings to 340B Covered Entities' (2016-09-12), citing a Medicines360 pricing announcement. Independently corroborated by a second, undated source describing Liletta's '340B federal pricing' as $50 (checked 2026-09-10), though that source also does not resolve whether the price was later raised to $100.
notes: STALE PRICE WARNING remains: both sources found describe the $50 price without a current (2026) date, and neither confirms or denies the reported later increase to $100. Two independently-worded sources agreeing on $50 is modestly reassuring but is not the same as a current price list. Needs direct verification against Medicines360's current price list before use. Relevant because the hospital in this model's real MRF extract (Denver Health) is a safety-net/DSH hospital and is plausibly, but not confirmedly, 340B-eligible.

description: Denver Health's own published self-pay/discounted-cash price for HCPCS J7297 (levonorgestrel IUD, 52mg, 8yr), from its CMS-mandated price-transparency machine-readable file
source: Denver Health and Hospital Authority standard-charges MRF, downloaded directly 2026-09-10 from https://sthpiprd.blob.core.windows.net/machine-readable-files/7840/841343242_denver-health-and-hospital-authority_standardcharges.csv (file dated 2026-04-30); gross charge $2,393.32, discounted-cash $837.67, inpatient negotiated-equivalent $820.91
notes: Directly verified, single-institution primary source -- not a national estimate. Provided as a cross-check ceiling, NOT the base-case acquisition cost: chargemaster/cash prices include hospital margin above true acquisition cost, which is exactly why iud_device_acquisition_cost_gpo and _340b (far lower) are used for the actual cost-minimization base case.

description: Incremental operating-room minutes for IUD insertion performed at the time of bariatric surgery
source: General (non-bariatric-specific) IUD-under-anesthesia literature: Children's Hospital Colorado / CU Anschutz adolescent-gynecology 'IUD Placement Under Anesthesia' patient-care protocol, stating the insertion itself takes 5-15 minutes.
notes: No published study of IUD insertion added-time specifically during bariatric surgery was found despite multiple targeted literature searches (2026-09-10). This is a general-population proxy, exactly analogous to how the sibling Lynch-syndrome model used non-Lynch-specific literature for its office-EMB failure-rate parameter. Revisit if a bariatric-specific timed study is ever published.

description: Scenario toggle: is IUD insertion at time of bariatric surgery billed as a separate professional fee (e.g. a different proceduralist, modifier -59/XU), or bundled/not separately billable because it is a minor procedure added to an already-open case?
source: Model-owner structural assumption, not yet confirmed against a specific payer's bundling policy or a real claim. Default FALSE (bundled/no separate fee) is the more conservative assumption for the combined arm's cost advantage, since it means the combined arm's professional-fee savings are as large as possible.
notes: Toggle to TRUE to test the scenario where the combined arm still incurs iud_insertion_professional_fee separately.
